name: Okolod
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists known (Lobel 2016, 7 pp; Prentice 1971; Spitzack 1984); no phonological description located

sources.note: Classification and speaker count only (cites Ethnologue 18th ed.); no phonology.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2016. North Borneo Sourcebook: Vocabularies and Functors. PALI Language Texts: Southeast Asia. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. Language 29 'Kolod (KOLOD, Murutic subgroup)', language information p. 49; wordlist rows '29. KOLOD' pp. 100ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Data from Long Tengoa (Sarawak), Solob (Sipitang, Sabah) and Pak Lo (Malinau, Kalimantan Utara); pronoun, demonstrative and case-marker tables plus a 500-item wordlist and 94 functors, no stress marking; the strings 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the book.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. 2013 (rev.). Dusun-Murut vowel harmony. ICAL paper, pre-publication version, DIU website.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not mention Kolod/Okolod; stress remarks (§4, penultimate stress in Labuk Kadazan, penultimate-or-final in Kimaragang) concern Dusunic languages only.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (xx+422 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Kolod: Kolod appears only in comparative/functor tables and in the focus-system discussion (p. 150). The only stress section (§8.2.9 Contrastive accent, p. 259) concerns Manide and Inagta Alabat (Philippines).

sources.citation: Spitzack, John A. 1984. The Murutic language family. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds), Languages of Sabah: a survey report, 155-223. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. §4.8 Kolod language, pp. 207-208 (PDF p. 53).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Survey of lexicostatistics and intelligibility; p. 208: 'Prentice (1971:300-303) has included a phonological and morphological outline for this language, but no other linguistic data is known for Kolod.' The words stress/accent do not occur in the chapter.

sources.citation: Prentice, D. J. 1971. The Murut languages of Sabah. Pacific Linguistics C-18. Canberra: ANU. §10.4 'The Okolod Murut language', pp. 300-303 (PDF pp. 312-315); §10.4.1 Phonology pp. 301-302.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Okolod. §10.4.1 gives the phoneme inventory /p t k ʔ b d g m n ŋ s l y w i u o a/, notes /b d g/ are never fricativised, no homorganic nasal+voiced stop sequences, and first-syllable vowel lengthening in roots with /o/ in both syllables (/doonoʔ/ 'one'); no word on stress. The book's stress statement (§2.2.1, p. 14: 'Stress appears to be non-phonemic in Timugon.. Strong stress.. occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word') is explicitly about Timugon, and §10.0 (p. 274) says the outline studies note only features differing from Timugon, so silence cannot be read as a claim.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. Language classification in Sarawak: a status report. Sarawak Museum Journal pre-publication PDF (DIU website).
sources.note: Okolod named once in a classification list ('E.1. Murut-Tidong (incl. Sabah Murut, Tagal, Okolod)'); no stress or phonology remarks.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Southwest Sabah revisited. Oceanic Linguistics 52(1): 36-68.

sources.note: Comparative/subgrouping article; the only modern comparative treatment that includes Kolod as a Murutic language with new field data; may contain phonological notes, though its focus is subgrouping and it is unlikely to state stress.

sources.citation: Genderen Stort, P. van. 1916. Nederlandsch-Tidoengsch-Tinggalan Dajaksche woordenlijst. Verhandelingen van het Koninklijk Bataviaasch Genootschap van Kunsten en Wetenschappen 61(5).

sources.note: Prentice 1971: 303 identifies the 'Sedalir' list in this work as 'a speech-form very similar to Okolod'; a wordlist, so almost certainly silent on stress, but the oldest Okolod-like record.

sources.citation: 'Murut Language Variation in Sipitang Sabah' (academia.edu 121081694; authors and venue not retrievable, Malaysian journal article).

sources.note: Sipitang district is one of the two Sabah Kolod areas (Lobel 2016 elicited at Solob, Sipitang); a variation study there could contain the first phonological notes on Kolod, possibly including stress.

sources.citation: SIL Malaysia Branch, unpublished Kolod wordlist (Baru Jumpa, Tenom area), cited in Spitzack 1984: 208, 223 n.52 as 'SIL's Kolod wordlist'.
